3-4: Two jugs and a tap: a given amount by filling, emptying and pouring.
A balance and a few weights, on one pan or on both: which loads can be weighed in one weighing.
One lighter fake among a few coins: the fewest weighings that are sure to find it.
Pouring from a bucket into a jug until the jug is full: what is left.
Bags of coins, one bag of heavier coins: a different number of coins from each bag, weighed once on a scale.
Sand timers of a few minutes each: how to measure a time neither of them shows alone.
Three parcels of different weights: two weighings that put them in order.
A fake that may be heavier or lighter, nobody knows which, among three coins: the weighings it takes.
Sharing water equally with jugs that have no marks.
Flour weighed out in halves: one bag split again and again on a balance.
A balance with arms of different lengths and one true weight: balance the weight against sand, then pour flour in its place until the sand balances again, and the flour weighs as much as the weight.
A scale whose needle is off by the same amount every time: weighing two things apart and then together shows the error, and from it each true weight.
A jug of known size and a jug that holds one of two sizes, with no way to see how much is in a jug: pourings that end differently for the two sizes show which it is.
5-6: Three buckets and a tap: the steps to a given amount.
Four parcels of different weights: the fewest weighings to put them in order.
A balance that holds only a few items on each pan, with one lighter fake.
Three sacks weighed two at a time: the weight of each from the three weighings.
Two fakes among a few coins: how many weighings find both.
One lighter fake among nine rings: what a given first weighing tells.
Stones of different weights: the fewest weighings to find the heaviest.
A fake that may be lighter or heavier, among a few coins.
A full jug shared into two equal halves with two smaller jugs.
Weights that go up in powers of two or of three: which loads one set can weigh.
A spoonful poured from one glass into another and a spoonful of the mix poured back: each glass holds what it held at first, so it has as much of the other drink as it lost of its own.
One fake among coins in three equal groups of several each, heavier or lighter, nobody knows which: two weighings, the second against a group shown to be real, tell only which, not the coin.
Weights or coins that should weigh as many grams as their labels say, one of them off: groups whose labels add up to the same total, made up with ones known to be right, find it.
Three piles of coins of different sizes, one fake coin in one of them: one weighing of the smallest pile against as many coins of another names a pile with no fake.
Four coins in a row, all real ones before all fakes, which are lighter, and some of each: one weighing of well-chosen coins tells which are fake, since it has three outcomes for the three cases.
Weights of 1, 2, 3 and so on, two of them on one pan: the pairs no other two can balance are those whose sum no other pair makes, the two smallest sums and the two largest.
Coins of two kinds with one fake among them, lighter if it is of one kind and heavier if of the other: both kinds on both pans, so that each outcome leaves about a third of the suspects.
